Google DeepMind reported that it is collaborating with the Singapore Government on a fine-tuned AI model aimed at detecting scams. According to the company, the work involves GovTech Singapore and uses lightweight Gemma models that run on-device to intercept conversational scams in private chats. The only report in this coverage came from Google DeepMind itself, so the account reflects the company's own description of the project. No independent outlet's reporting is included here.
editorial.whyItMatters: The project shows frontier AI developers working with a government on targeted, privacy-focused tools against fraud. It is a narrow application of AI rather than a development toward more general capabilities.

The company named GovTech Singapore as a partner in the work.

The company said the approach involves zero cloud data egress.
